Record Class PageParams

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
org.jwcarman.jpa.spring.web.PageParams
Record Components:
pageIndex - the zero-based page number, may be null (defaults to 0)
pageSize - the number of items per page, may be null (defaults to 20)
sortBy - the sort field name as string (e.g., "LAST_NAME"), may be null for unsorted
sortDirection - the sort direction (ASC or DESC), may be null (defaults to ASC)
All Implemented Interfaces:
PageSpec
public record PageParams(Integer pageIndex, Integer pageSize, String sortBy, SortDirection sortDirection) extends Record implements PageSpec
Spring Web query parameter binding class for pagination requests.

This class implements PageSpec and is designed to automatically bind query parameters to pagination settings in Spring REST controllers. All fields are optional, allowing flexible pagination requests. Simply add as a method parameter - Spring will automatically bind the query parameters.

Usage in REST Controllers

Basic Usage

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/persons")
public class PersonController {

    @Autowired
    private PersonService personService;

    @GetMapping
    public PageDto<PersonDto> getPersons(PageParams pageParams) {
        // Spring automatically binds query parameters to pageParams
        return personService.findAll(pageParams);
    }
}

// Example URLs:
// GET /api/persons?pageIndex=0&pageSize=10&sortBy=LAST_NAME&sortDirection=ASC
// GET /api/persons?pageIndex=1&pageSize=25&sortBy=CREATED&sortDirection=DESC
// GET /api/persons (all parameters optional, uses defaults)

With Search Parameters

@GetMapping
public PageDto<PersonDto> searchPersons(
        @RequestParam(required = false) String query,
        PageParams pageParams) {
    return personService.search(query, pageParams);
}

// Example URLs:
// GET /api/persons?query=john&pageIndex=0&pageSize=20&sortBy=LAST_NAME&sortDirection=ASC
// GET /api/persons?query=smith&pageSize=10

Service Layer Integration

@Service
public class PersonService {

    private static final Paginator PAGINATOR = Paginator.of(Person.class, PersonSort.class);

    @Autowired
    private PersonRepository personRepository;

    public PageDto<PersonDto> findAll(PageSpec pageSpec) {
        // Paginator resolves the sort field, queries, and converts to DTOs
        return PAGINATOR.paginate(pageSpec, personRepository::findAll, PersonDto::fromEntity);
    }
}

Query Parameter Mapping

The following query parameters are automatically bound:

  • pageIndex - Zero-based page number (e.g., 0, 1, 2...)
  • pageSize - Number of items per page (e.g., 10, 20, 50...)
  • sortBy - Sort field name as string (e.g., "LAST_NAME", "CREATED")
  • sortDirection - Sort direction: "ASC" or "DESC"

Testing

Create instances using the canonical constructor:

@Test
void shouldPaginateResults() {
    PageParams params = new PageParams(0, 25, "LAST_NAME", SortDirection.DESC);

    PageDto<PersonDto> result = personService.findAll(params);

    assertThat(result.pagination().pageIndex()).isZero();
    assertThat(result.pagination().pageSize()).isEqualTo(25);
}

@Test
void shouldUseDefaults() {
    PageParams params = new PageParams(null, null, null, null);

    PageDto<PersonDto> result = personService.findAll(params);

    // Uses Paginator defaults (page 0, size 20, sorted by the "id" tiebreaker)
    assertThat(result.pagination().pageIndex()).isZero();
    assertThat(result.pagination().pageSize()).isEqualTo(20);
}

Custom Parameter Names

If you need different URL parameter names (e.g., page instead of pageIndex), use individual @RequestParam annotations and build the PageParams manually:

@GetMapping
public PageDto<PersonDto> getPersons(
        @RequestParam(required = false) Integer page,
        @RequestParam(required = false) Integer size,
        @RequestParam(required = false) String sortBy,
        @RequestParam(required = false) SortDirection sortDirection) {

    PageParams params = new PageParams(page, size, sortBy, sortDirection);

    return personService.findAll(params);
}

// Example URLs:
// GET /api/persons?page=0&size=10&sortBy=LAST_NAME&sortDirection=ASC
